title: Mixing times and spectra of non-equilibrium symmetric exclusion processes on general graphs
summary: The symmetric exclusion process (SEP) is a classical model of interacting particles on a graph, in which multiple particles execute random walks subject to the constraint that no two particles may occupy the same vertex. The version of the process in which the number of particles is fixed, is by now very well understood, through the study of reversible Markov chains. In this paper, we study the non-equilibrium version of the SEP, in which some vertices of the graph interact with external heat baths, held at different temperatures, that mediate transport through the graph.
